sources_considered.why: CNBC report (syndicated) of Pichai's DealBook remarks. It also carries Altman's contrary 'no wall' remark.
Syndicated copy of the November 2024 Reuters report quoting Sutskever.
Transcript of Nadella's Ignite keynote, which shows his actual framing.

receipt.public_excerpt: "I think the progress is going to get harder. When I look at [2025], the low-hanging fruit is gone," said Pichai, adding: "The hill is steeper ... You're definitely going to need deeper breakthroughs as we get to the next stage."

evidence_items.explanation: Pichai said in early December 2024 that progress is getting harder and deeper breakthroughs are needed. This matches the Pichai part of the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: Ilya Sutskever, co-founder of AI labs Safe Superintelligence (SSI) and OpenAI, told Reuters recently that results from scaling up pre-training - the phase of training an AI model that use s a vast amount of unlabeled data to understand language patterns and structures - have plateaued.

evidence_items.explanation: Major reporting in November 2024 said the results of pre-training scaling had plateaued and that labs were looking for new methods. This supports 'by most accounts, scaling has begun to diminish.'

evidence_items.explanation: Nadella acknowledged the debate and said skepticism would spur innovation in model architectures. He also said 'we are seeing the emergence of a new scaling law.' So the Nadella part only partly fits Marcus's description.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, for example, posted "there is no wall" on social media platform X in November

evidence_items.explanation: A leading figure publicly disputed that scaling had hit a wall. This shows the view was contested, though the claim only says 'by most accounts.'

unresolved_gaps: 'Most accounts' cannot be counted. The judgment rests on prominent reporting, not a survey.
Nadella's own words stress a new test-time scaling law more than a need for breakthroughs.
